sourceQualifications.qualification: Practical losses and maintained forced steady state; sinusoidal forcing with time-invariant linear response, not a universal assertion about alternating waveforms.
Complete historical CRT/mains and 50/60-hertz account, descriptive and explicitly not live-outlet instructions; complete cycles distinguished from directional half-cycles.
Mean drift in an approximately constant-property ohmic conductor with linear quasistatic behavior and short carrier-response time; no instantaneous resistor relation imposed on general RLC circuits.
Finite field propagation; propagation time much shorter than period and negligible distributed charge accumulation for equal instantaneous current in the same unbranched lumped circuit.
Single-turn planar loop in uniform field, chosen normal-to-B angle, constant-rotation/zero-angle time origin, oriented flux/emf convention, and exact negative time derivative.
omega is angular frequency in radians per second; f is ordinary frequency in cycles per second/hertz, related by the prose explanation of twice pi.
Footnote remains N21-owned. A common initial-phase/time-origin choice never removes relative phase; preserved plus-varphi convention means current phase minus voltage phase.
